A0225.title: Physical-World Prompt Injection Detection
A0225.definition: Detection of physical-world prompt-injection attacks against embodied-intelligence VLA models via environment-consistency checking, anomalous-visual-cue identification, and action-intent auditing.
A0225.description: Physical-world prompt injection detection targets attack vectors where adversaries place visual cues (stickers, printed patterns, occlusions, projections) in the robot's operating environment to mislead VLA models into misinterpreting instructions. It establishes detection capabilities across three dimensions. First, environmental consistency verification compares instructions parsed by the VLM against registered legitimate instruction sources (operator voice/text/predefined tasks), downgrading or rejecting instructions from unverified origins. Second, anomalous visual cue recognition detects suddenly appearing high-contrast text, unnaturally arranged patterns, task-irrelevant signage, and other suspicious injection carriers in the scene. Third, action intent auditing validates whether the VLA's output action sequence aligns with the current task context and safety boundaries before execution, triggering secondary confirmation for intent deviations. This approach is a key differentiator for embodied intelligence compared to pure software prompt injection defense, as injection carriers exist in the physical world and cannot be fully eliminated by input filtering alone, requiring defense-in-depth that combines environmental perception with action-layer validation. It complements A0178 (AIoT model security protection) and A0014 (tamper-proof mechanisms), with the former focusing on model-layer robustness while this measure targets injection carrier identification in the physical world.
A0225.limitation: It is infeasible to exhaustively enumerate all injection forms, as novel adversarial examples can bypass the detector. Dynamic physical environment variations (illumination, occlusion, viewpoint) lead to high false positive rates. The detector itself may be deceived by adversarial attacks. A trade-off exists between real-time requirements and detection overhead, making deployment infeasible in all scenarios.

references.title: Misleading text in the physical world can hijack AI-enabled robots - UC Santa Cruz
